hypotheses.justification: The statement only needs `MinData.E K 5`, which requires `[CommRing K]`, so `CharP K 2` is not needed to state it. It is also true in every characteristic. `MinData.E R k = toEnd R d (op k)`, and `Minuscule.toEnd_single` gives `E (single a 1) = digVec R d (dig (op k) a)`. `digVec` is `0` whenever its code `c` is `< 2`, by `digVec_of_lt_two`. `tgt_eq` (no field hypothesis) gives `tgt k j = dig (op k) j / 2`, and `tgt_e1.2.1 : tgt 5 1 = 0` makes `dig (op 5) 1 < 2`. So the value is `0` in any commutative ring. The current proof goes through `E_single_zero`, `coe_E` and `toMatrix_E`, which need `CharP K 2`. Replace it with `rw [MinData.E, Minuscule.toEnd_single]`, rewrite with `tgt_eq`, and close with `digVec_of_lt_two`. Deleting `[CharP K 2]` and `[Finite K]` together works.

`Finite K` appears nowhere in the statement, and neither the proof nor the lemmas it uses (`E_single_zero`, `coe_E`, `toMatrix_E`) need it. Only `Field K` is needed for `e6Data.E K 5`, and the alternative argument through `digVec_of_lt_two` also never uses finiteness. It can be deleted on its own, and also together with `[CharP K 2]`.
